comment: 🔴 37L.6 — the high-water mark for English left in the markup, by surface. A number may only go DOWN. `verify:sprint37l` fails when one rises, which is the half that stops C182 happening for a fourth time: sprints 19, 21 and 31 each shipped real Arabic work and none of them counted what was left, so fourteen sprints wrote English past a rule. Lowering these is the work. Raising one is a decision somebody makes on purpose, in a diff, with a reason in PLAN.md.
loweredInSprint51: 🔴 admin 301 to 297 and shared 79 to 71 is a MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, not translation work, and the difference matters. `literalsIn` matched the `>` of an arrow function followed by a type argument, so `(fn: () => Promise<State>)` counted as a visible literal named `Promise`. Twelve phantoms across seven files. Sprint 51's first instinct was to rewrite real code to please the regex, which is how a bad ratchet makes a codebase worse. `verify:sprint51` now asserts both halves: the arrow forms do not count, and five shapes of genuine literal still do, so the scanner is corrected rather than blinded.
note: The count is a FLOOR, not a total: it sees JSX text nodes and four attributes, so a string inside a ternary or passed as an ordinary prop is invisible to it. It is still the right ratchet, because it cannot be satisfied by remembering and it moves the moment somebody types a sentence into a page.

overridability.comment: 🔴 45.7 — the OTHER number, and the one C217 was actually about. A literal count says how much English is left; it says nothing about whether the English that IS translated can be changed by an administrator. Until 45.3 the answer for 72 client components was no: `I18nProvider` read the bundled dictionary and never consulted `ui_strings`, so an admin published an edit, saw the server-rendered half of a page change, and got no error on the other half. This counts components that read the dictionary as a VALUE instead of through a resolver. Zero is the only acceptable number: `useT` and `getI18n` both consult overrides, a direct `DICTIONARIES` read does not, and there is no case where bypassing is right.

loweredInSprint53: 🔴 patient 22→18, admin 297→294, shared 71→60 is a SECOND MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, of the same family as sprint 51's and found the same way: sprint 53 added a sponsor portal, the number went up, and reading WHY showed phantoms rather than English. `literalsIn` was matching the `>` of a relational operator inside a JSX expression container, so `{benefits.length > 1 ? (` captured the code between it and the next `<`, and a four-letter identifier in that code passed the letter test. Two real examples, both of which were IN the previous floor: "1 ? ( benefit.isPrimary ? (" and ") : canRequest && !open ? (". Rejected now by the punctuation only code has — `? (`, `) :`, `&&`, `||` — rather than by rejecting every parenthesis, which would also have dropped genuine prose like "VAT (14%)". VERIFIED THE SAME WAY THE FOUNDER VERIFIED SPRINT 51's: the corrected scanner was run against main at b66997b, which gave patient 18, auth 4, portal 1, admin 294, shared 60 — identical on every surface. So the drop is measurement and the sprint's own new surfaces add nothing to any floor. 🔴 And admin held at 294 rather than rising by twelve: the new operator screens for 53.6 are MessageKeys under `asponsor.`, because the rule from sprint 45 on is that a new string is a key, whatever the surrounding debt. One keyed label now sits in an admin nav of fifteen literals, which is that debt becoming visible rather than a new one.
